title: Company Objective Convergence Horizon and Dependency Fabric
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: We lack a single, operational mapping from company-level OKRs to the initiatives and owners across Eng/Design/Go-to-market. This causes duplicated effort, ambiguous ownership on cross-team dependencies, and ad-hoc escalation when priorities shift.

Goal: Design and roll out a reproducible playbook + lightweight tooling (OKR->Initiative matrix, dependency fabric, and tracking dashboard) that enables transparent alignment, predictable delivery windows, and faster resolution of cross-functional resource conflicts.

Scope: company-level OKRs for 2025 Q2–Q4, all outward-facing product and platform initiatives that affect latency, cost, reliability, Dedicated/Private features, Console observability, and Optimize tooling. Excludes low-touch infrastructure hygiene items (< 1 sprint impact).

Key outcomes:
- A canonical OKR->Initiative mapping with owners and explicit acceptance criteria per initiative.
- A cross-functional dependency register with priority, blocking severity, and mitigation options.
- A Metabase dashboard for live tracking (initiative status, SLO risk signals, committed release windows).
- A rollout plan for biweekly OKR sync cadence and an initiative contract template for tracking scope/rollback lanes.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical mapping doc published in Confluence with Objective->Outcome->Initiative rows and assigned owner for 95% of initiatives
Dependency register populated with top 30 cross-team dependencies and initial mitigation plans
Metabase tracking dashboard created with filters for objective, team, release window, and risk level
Biweekly cross-functional sync slot scheduled and first 3 meetings run with minutes posted
Two pilot initiatives (runtime autoscaling and console rollout UX) adopt the initiative-contract template and show measurable reduction in unplanned escalations
comments: 2025-02-15 | Aisha Kumar: Created initial RFC. Proposed three-tier mapping (Objective -> Outcome -> Initiative). Asked ENG and Design for feedback; initial invite list sent to eng-sr-leads@redwood.ai.

2025-02-19 | Liam Chen (assignee): Ran a quick audit of active initiatives across product and infra — consolidated 48 candidate initiatives down to 22 that directly map to company OKRs. Flagged several ambiguous owners for follow-up (noted in Confluence page).

2025-02-24 | Priya Rao (Eng Director): Feedback: prefer light-touch register with severity bands to avoid process overhead. Suggested capturing mitigation options rather than full runbooks for each dependency. Accepted for MVP. (See comment thread in Confluence)

2025-02-28 | Design Review (Sofia Martinez): Recommend adding UX metrics to acceptance criteria for Console initiatives (task added PM-100103). Will provide 2 exemplar mockups for pilot initiative-contracts.

2025-03-03 | Liam Chen: Pilot selection done — 'runtime autoscaling by tier' (ENG owner: Mateo Alvarez) and 'console rollout hub view' (Design owner: Sofia Martinez). Created initiative-contract drafts and posted links to PRs and mockups.

2025-03-04 | Aisha Kumar: Decision recorded — adopt biweekly 'OKR Convergence' sync on Tuesdays 09:30 PST. Each meeting to run 45 minutes with a published decision log and top-5 risk list. Action: Liam to schedule recurring invite and owner rotation.

2025-03-05 | Engineering feedback (Kofi Mensah): Raised a trade-off: finer-grained initiative mapping increases coordination cost; propose quarterly review cadence for non-critical dependencies. Tagged as 'deferred' for low-severity items.
notes:
Trade-offs discussed: (1) granularity vs. operational load — MVP will focus on top-line mapping with severity-banded dependencies; (2) tooling vs. manual process — initial cycle will use CSV + Metabase, then evaluate investment in an internal register UI.

Next steps: finish mapping owners for remaining 8 initiatives (owners pinged), finalize Metabase schema with Eng telemetry team (KPI list in Confluence), and run first pilot sync on 2025-03-11.
